# deoos

> Durable execution on object storage. One Rust server keeps workflow state in S3-compatible storage (RustFS in the examples). Python and TypeScript SDKs ship only as GitHub release archives, never as PyPI or npm packages. deoos is not DBOS and does not use Postgres.

deoos runs an ordinary function and remembers completed steps. A killed worker continues from the last committed step. Put each side effect in its own step. Replay returns the saved result and does not call the function again.

## Docs

- [Skill for coding agents](agents/SKILL.md): add deoos to a project, write a durable workflow, and debug a run
- [README](README.md): install from a GitHub release archive, library mode, and server mode
- [Agent feedback](docs/agent-feedback.md): how `deoos feedback` files a report and how to triage it
- [Examples](https://github.com/deoos-dev/deoos-examples): runnable workflows, including an order flow and a payment resume

## Install

Do not use `pip install deoos` or `npm install deoos`. Download the archive for your OS and CPU from the GitHub release, then install the wheel and the Node tarball from that archive. The archive also contains `llms.txt` and `agents/`.

## Run

From a clone:

```
make dev
export ENGINE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7331
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD/clients/python"
python -m deoos info
```

`info` prints `"protocol_version": 3` when the engine is up.

Server mode needs `ENGINE_URL` (and `ENGINE_TOKEN` when the server was started with one). Library mode needs `DEOOS_STORAGE_BUCKET` instead of a server. `DEOOS_MODE=library` ignores `ENGINE_URL`. `DEOOS_MODE=server` requires it.

## MCP

The MCP server is Python, over stdio, and it ships inside the release wheel. Coding agents launch it as a local process. It does not open a port and it does not run workers.

```
python -m deoos mcp --allow-actions
```

Read tools: `engine_health`, `docs_search`, `task_list`, `task_summary`, `task_history`.
Action tools (need `--allow-actions`): `task_submit`, `task_cancel`, `task_retry`, `task_signal`.
`feedback` is always available. It is a dry run unless `send` is true.

## Feedback

```
python -m deoos feedback --tried "what you tried" --happened "what happened"
python -m deoos feedback --send --tried "what you tried" --happened "what happened"
```

The first command prints the exact GitHub issue payload and files nothing. `--send` with `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` files an issue in `deoos-dev/deoos` labeled `agent-feedback`. Secret-like text is refused and is not echoed.

## Fresh-agent check

`evals/fresh-agent/README.md` is the harness that scores "add deoos and survive a crash mid-step" against a real engine.
